question: How does the self misrecognize its own expressions in the state of difference?
premises: One considers self-uttered statements as spoken by another
The thing to be taught and the means by which it is taught appear distinct
These distinctions arise within the same self
inference: In the differentiated state, the self attributes its own expressions and teachings to an other.
plain_english: One considers statements uttered by oneself as spoken by another; and the thing to be taught and that by which it is taught are likewise taken as distinct.
